description: Controlled vocabulary defining curing conditions used in the Concrete Grand Challenge Experimental Database.

entries.definition: Curing performed by exposing specimens to ambient air conditions.
Curing performed under elevated temperature and pressure in an autoclave.
Curing performed under controlled temperature, humidity, or environmental conditions.
Curing performed under field or in-situ exposure conditions.
Curing performed in a fog room or high-humidity moist-curing chamber.
Curing performed with externally applied heat or elevated temperature.
Curing performed in laboratory air under reported or unreported ambient laboratory conditions.
Curing performed by immersion in lime-saturated water.
Curing performed using a curing membrane or curing compound to limit moisture loss.
No explicit curing procedure was applied.
Curing performed under sealed conditions to prevent or reduce moisture exchange with the environment.
Curing performed under standard moist-curing conditions, as defined by the relevant testing standard or experimental protocol.
Curing performed using steam or a steam-curing chamber.
Curing performed by immersion in water or continuous exposure to water.
Curing condition that does not fall within the predefined categories.
Curing condition not reported or not identifiable from the available documentation.
